arguments.value: 28-year-old man with hypertension, dyslipidemia, and prior surgical ASD closure presented with recurrent chest pain. Initial angiography in 2016 showed only mild proximal LAD stenosis, but in 2023 repeat angiography revealed severe proximal-to-mid LAD stenosis with twisting channels. OCT demonstrated two separate lumens with multiple microchannels and no communication between the main channels, consistent with woven coronary artery in the LAD, likely acquired from recanalized thrombus. He underwent successful PCI with stent implantation and remained event-free at 1-year follow-up.
